authority.canonicalSource: Live attached October MCP tools/list plus installed October adapter generator
authority.rule: October defines these capabilities. YURI indexes and validates a versioned projection; it does not redefine the implementations or persist transient canvas/node identities.

tools.name: add_chat
tools.description: Add an AI chat node to the canvas (a conversational coding agent). Like add_terminal, you can use this to bring on a helper agent — a chat node is better when the subtask wants a back-and-forth the user can watch and steer. The new chat is auto-connected to you, so coordinate via message_peer / send_to_node. Pass `harness` to choose the engine (claude-code / codex / opencode / hermes / cursor / grok); defaults to the user's default.
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Drop a sticky note on the canvas (instructions, a TODO, a reminder for the user or other agents).
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: add_remotion
tools.description: Add a Remotion video block to the canvas (a programmatic video project + live Studio preview).
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: add_screen
tools.description: Add a screen (live preview) to the canvas. kind "desktop" = a web page, "phone" = a mobile screen. It scaffolds a real route/file you can then edit.
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: add_task
tools.description: Post a task to this canvas's shared board for any connected agent (including yourself) to pick up. Use it to break work into parallelizable pieces or to hand off follow-ups without addressing a specific peer. Keep the description self-contained — the claimer may have none of your context. Optional `after` lists task ids that must finish first (the task stays blocked until they do). Returns the new task id.

after.description: task ids that must complete before this one is claimable

tools.stateEffect: mutates shared task-board state

tools.name: add_terminal
tools.description: Add a terminal to the canvas — including to SPAWN A HELPER AGENT for a parallelizable subtask. You are not limited to working alone: when a task splits into independent parts, add a terminal per part with `agent` set, then drive each with send_to_node and coordinate via message_peer (the new terminal is auto-connected to you, so you can message it right away). Pass `agent` (claude / codex / opencode / hermes / cursor / grok) to AUTO-START that coding agent — e.g. "add 3 claude code terminals" → call this 3× with agent:"claude". For several agents on the SAME repo at once, set `isolate:true` (each gets its own git worktree+branch, no collisions). Omit `agent` for a plain shell. Optionally pass cwd (an absolute folder); it defaults to the workspace folder so the agent boots immediately (omit only to let the user pick a folder, which delays launch).

agent.description: coding agent to auto-launch in the terminal

cwd.description: absolute folder to open the terminal in

isolate.description: run this agent in its OWN git worktree+branch so several agents can work the SAME repo in parallel without colliding. Use when fanning out multiple agents on one codebase.

tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: arrange_nodes
tools.description: Tidy the layout: lay nodes out in a grid. Pass `ids` to arrange specific nodes (in order), or omit to arrange everything. `columns` sets the grid width (default 3).

ids.description: node ids to arrange, in order; omit for all

tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the human user a question and wait for their answer. Use before any large, irreversible, or ambiguous change — confirm your approach, or let them choose between valid options (e.g. two designs, which files to touch). Provide 2–4 short `options` when it is a choice; omit them for an open question. Blocks until they reply, then returns their answer. Prefer asking over guessing on consequential decisions; do not ask about trivial, easily-reversible details.

question.description: the question to show the user

tools.stateEffect: asks or speaks to the user

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element in the connected browser by CSS selector OR an @ref from browser_snapshot/browser_find (a trusted click at its center, so framework handlers fire; @refs reach into shadow DOM + same-origin iframes). Returns whether an element matched.

selector.description: CSS selector (e.g. button[type=submit]) or an @ref like @5 from browser_snapshot/find

tools.stateEffect: changes connected browser state or submits page input

tools.name: browser_eval
tools.description: Evaluate arbitrary JavaScript in the connected browser page and return the result. Powerful but unrestricted — the user is asked to confirm before it runs.

code.description: JavaScript expression/statements to run in the page

tools.stateEffect: changes connected browser state or submits page input

tools.name: browser_find
tools.description: Find a clickable element in the connected browser by its visible text (case-insensitive) and get a CSS selector you can pass to browser_click. Use when you know the button/link label but not its selector.

text.description: visible text of the element, e.g. "Watch" or "Sign in"

tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: browser_get_console
tools.description: Get recent console messages (logs/warnings/errors) from the connected browser — useful to reproduce bugs.
tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: browser_get_downloads
tools.description: List recent files the connected browser downloaded (filename, state, save path in your Downloads folder).
tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: browser_get_network
tools.description: Get recent network requests (method, status, type, URL) from the connected browser. Capture starts when an agent is wired in or on first call. Pass `body` (a URL substring) to fetch the response BODY of the most recent matching request — for reverse-engineering an API or debugging a failed response. Body reads ask the user first and have obvious secrets (tokens/cookies) redacted + the body capped.

body.description: a URL substring; returns that request’s response body instead of the list

tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate the connected browser to a URL (http/https). Returns the URL it landed on.

url.description: absolute URL to open, e.g. https://example.com

tools.stateEffect: changes connected browser state or submits page input

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description: Press a single key in the connected browser (e.g. Enter, Tab, Escape).
tools.stateEffect: changes connected browser state or submits page input

tools.name: browser_read
tools.description: Read the current page of the browser wired to you: its title, URL and visible text. Use this to summarize a page, pull reference content, or check what's on screen after navigating/clicking.
tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Take a PNG screenshot of the connected browser viewport. Use when you need to SEE the page (layout, images, canvas) — prefer browser_read for plain text.
tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the connected browser: up, down, top or bottom.
tools.stateEffect: changes connected browser state or submits page input

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: List the visible interactive elements (links, buttons, inputs) on the connected page with their text and CSS selectors — a cheap, token-light alternative to a screenshot for deciding what to click/type.
tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type text into an input/textarea in the connected browser by CSS selector OR an @ref from browser_snapshot/browser_find (React-controlled-input safe). Returns whether an element matched.

selector.description: CSS selector or an @ref like @5 from browser_snapshot/find

tools.stateEffect: changes connected browser state or submits page input

tools.name: browser_upload
tools.description: Attach a local file to a <input type=file> in the connected browser (by CSS selector) so the page can upload it. The user is asked to confirm before the file is attached.

path.description: absolute path of the local file to attach

selector.description: CSS selector of the file input (light DOM)

tools.stateEffect: changes connected browser state or submits page input

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description: Wait until a CSS selector appears in the connected browser, or wait a fixed number of milliseconds. Use after a navigation/click that loads content. Returns whether the wait was satisfied.

ms.description: fixed wait in milliseconds (if no selector)

tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: check_inbox
tools.description: Pull anything new from your connected peers right now: every message addressed to you (all of them, delivered together — messages that arrived while you were busy are queued and drained as one batch) plus a short note of what peers recently did. (October also surfaces these automatically at the start of your turn.)
tools.stateEffect: consumes queued inbox entries

tools.name: claim_task
tools.description: Claim a task from the shared board before working on it — the claim is atomic, so no other agent can take it once it's yours. Call with a task id to claim that task, or with no id to claim the oldest unblocked open task. Claiming tells everyone the work is covered; do the work, then call complete_task. A claim held by an agent that went offline can be re-claimed.

id.description: task id to claim; omit for the next available task

tools.stateEffect: mutates shared task-board state

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Mark a board task done, optionally with a short note of the outcome (where the result lives, anything the next task needs). Completing a task automatically unblocks tasks that depended on it. Only complete work that is actually done and verified.

note.description: one-line outcome — where the result is, caveats

tools.stateEffect: mutates shared task-board state

tools.name: connect_nodes
tools.description: Draw a connection between two canvas nodes (ids from list_canvas) — e.g. a chat → a screen, or a terminal → a screen. Connecting two AGENTS makes them peers on the bus so they can message_peer each other (agents you spawn via add_terminal/add_chat are already connected to you; use this to wire up agents that were added separately).
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: create_plan
tools.description: Lay out a multi-step plan as a live checklist the user watches tick off. REQUIRED whenever the user asks for several things at once (3+ distinct steps — e.g. "do these 10 things", "spin up the whole project"). Pass `items`: an ordered array of short step descriptions. After creating it, drive EVERY item to completion via update_plan_item — never stop after the first few.

items.description: ordered list of short step descriptions

tools.stateEffect: mutates visible plan state

tools.name: disconnect_nodes
tools.description: Remove the connection between two canvas nodes (ids from list_canvas).
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: find
tools.description: Find files in the canvas workspace by MEANING or behaviour — not just filename. e.g. "the file that handles auth redirects", "where the pricing CTA is rendered", "what changed recently". Returns ranked paths, each with a one-line reason and the last commit that touched it. Use this instead of guessing paths.

query.description: natural-language description of the file(s) you want to locate

tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: get_node_status
tools.description: Check whether a worker agent is busy or idle, by name (e.g. "Atlas") or id — instant, and it does NOT interrupt them. Chat agents report precise busy/idle; terminal agents report whether a command is running / waiting for input. Pass `history: true` to also get a short journal of what that agent has been doing lately (its recent per-turn summaries) — use it to answer "what has X been up to?" without messaging them. Use before sending dependent work or to report progress to the user.

history.description: also return the agent's recent turn-by-turn activity journal

tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: get_peer_context
tools.description: Get the fuller recent context of your connected peers (what they have been working on). Optionally pass a peer name to focus on one.

peer.description: peer display name (optional; omit for all peers)

tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: import_sessions
tools.description: Bring the user's EXISTING Claude Code / Codex conversations from this machine onto the canvas: October scans the CLIs' own session transcripts on disk (newest first, skipping sessions October already tracks), and spawns one terminal per session resumed in its original folder (`claude --resume <id>` / `codex resume <id>`). Use when the user asks to bring/import/resume their sessions. The result names what was resumed and how many more exist.

count.description: how many to bring in (default 5, newest first)

tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: install_video_tools
tools.description: Make the LOCAL video toolchain ready — downloads a static, libass-enabled ffmpeg to October’s app data on first use (no Homebrew, works on macOS + Windows). Reuses a system ffmpeg when one is already on PATH (no download; skips confirmation in that case). Returns whether ffmpeg is now ready, or guidance when the platform has no auto-install path. Fully local, free, no cloud — ffmpeg burns ASS subtitles and mixes background music for the deterministic captions/BGM pipeline.
tools.stateEffect: installs tooling or starts/stops a local process

tools.name: list_canvas
tools.description: List the nodes on your canvas (screens, chats, terminals/agents by NAME, notes, video blocks) AND the connections between them. Use this to see who is wired to whom; use list_peers for just the peers connected to YOU. Use the ids with move_node / connect_nodes.
tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: list_peers
tools.description: List the sessions you are connected to on the canvas, with their latest status and one-line summary.
tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: See this canvas's shared task board: every task with its status (open / claimed / done), who claimed it, and whether it's still blocked by dependencies. Check it when you finish something or have spare capacity — unclaimed open tasks are work anyone can pick up with claim_task.
tools.stateEffect: none

tools.name: message_peer
tools.description: Talk to a connected peer agent — address them by name (e.g. "Marshall"). This is the one way you reach a peer: ask a question, answer one, hand off a task, share a finding, debate, or just reply. Your message is delivered VERBATIM and the peer responds on its own — no need to phrase it as a command. If the peer is mid-task, your message is queued and delivered together with anything else waiting the moment they are free — so send once and do NOT retry or take over their work; say "no reply needed" in the message when that is the intent, otherwise a reply is expected. Address them by name (check list_peers if unsure who is connected); reply to a peer who messaged you by sending back to their name. To reach several peers at once, pass a comma-separated list ("Atlas, Orion") or the word "all" (every connected peer) — each recipient gets the same verbatim message. Only reach out when you have something substantive — a real answer, a needed question, or work to hand off. If an exchange is going in circles, or your task is done and there is nothing to pass on, send nothing: staying silent is how a multi-agent loop is meant to end.

message.description: what to say — your exact words, delivered verbatim

peer.description: one peer name (e.g. "Marshall") or kind ("terminal"/"chat"); or a comma list / "all" to reach several

tools.stateEffect: delivers a message or queued prompt

tools.name: move_node
tools.description: Reposition a canvas node (use an id from list_canvas).
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: remove_node
tools.description: Delete a canvas node and its connections (use an id from list_canvas). Closes a terminal/agent it was running.
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: rename_node
tools.description: Rename a canvas node (use an id from list_canvas). For a terminal/chat this sets the agent's name (e.g. "Marshall"); for a screen it sets the title.
tools.stateEffect: mutates canvas or launches/removes a session

tools.name: send_to_node
tools.description: Send text to a node (id from list_canvas): for a TERMINAL it is delivered as a queued October message — handed to the agent when it can actually receive it (immediately if idle; after its current task / pending prompt otherwise), never typed over a busy session; for a CHAT it posts the message and runs the agent; for a VIDEO EDITOR it hands the task to the video agent wired to that editor (spawning + connecting one if none is). This is how you DRIVE agents, e.g. "add 3 claude terminals and have each refactor a different module". The result says whether it delivered now or was queued.
tools.stateEffect: delivers a message or queued prompt

tools.name: speak
tools.description: Say a SHORT spoken confirmation back to the user (one sentence). Only audible when the command arrived by voice/wake-word (ignored for typed commands), so use it freely to confirm hands-free actions, e.g. "Connected Atlas to Orion and started two agents." Do not narrate every tool call — speak once when a request (or plan) is done, or to ask a quick spoken question.
tools.stateEffect: asks or speaks to the user

tools.name: start_dev_server
tools.description: Start (run) the app's dev server so screens show a live preview. Optionally pass `path` (a workspace app folder); defaults to the project.
tools.stateEffect: installs tooling or starts/stops a local process

tools.name: stop_dev_server
tools.description: Stop the app's dev server. Optionally pass `path`; defaults to the project.
tools.stateEffect: installs tooling or starts/stops a local process

tools.name: update_plan_item
tools.description: Update one plan item as you go: set it in_progress when you start, done when finished, or blocked (with a note) if you truly cannot. Keep the checklist honest so the user sees real progress. Keep calling this until every item is done or blocked.
tools.stateEffect: mutates visible plan state

tools.name: wait_for_nodes
tools.description: Block until the named worker agents finish their current work (go idle), then return their status. Use this to SEQUENCE dependent work — e.g. wait for Atlas to finish the API before telling Orion to build the UI against it. Pass `names` (agent names or ids). Polls up to `timeout_sec` (default 120, max 600). Chat agents give the most reliable completion signal.

names.description: agent names or node ids to wait for

tools.stateEffect: none

Report a completed turn excerpt for October status and summary handling.
Report attached harness session live/offline state and resumable session identity where supported.
Raise the terminal needs-user-attention signal for approval or notification events.

versionedFindings.symptom: The generated pre-prompt command can be killed by the 5-second outer hook timeout and shown as a hook failure.
versionedFindings.cause: pullInjection fetches /hook/pre-prompt without an internal AbortSignal deadline; a stalled October event loop outlives the outer hook budget.
versionedFindings.evidence: A controlled stalled-loopback fixture remained blocked at 5200ms and required SIGTERM; healthy live, missing-env, and closed-port fixtures exited 0.
versionedFindings.requiredFix: Use a fail-soft internal request deadline materially shorter than every outer harness timeout, emit nothing on timeout, and add a stalled-server regression fixture. Do not hand-edit ~/.october/bus-hook.mjs because October regenerates it.
